title: Hardcoded Supabase service-role key, NEXT_PUBLIC-exposed to the browser
evidence: SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is a hardcoded service_role JWT fallback (decoded role:service_role) read from NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY — the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix bundles this credential into the browser. It bypasses all RLS.
impact: Anyone loading the app obtains a full-RLS-bypass credential to the database.
fix: Never prefix service-role with NEXT_PUBLIC_; keep it server-only and rotate.

title: Row Level Security disabled on every table
evidence: alter table ... disable row level security on profiles/notes/shares/api_tokens (0001_init.sql:38-41). With RLS off and no policies, every row is reachable via the anon key.
impact: Complete cross-tenant exposure of all four tables via PostgREST.
fix: Enable RLS and add owner-scoped policies on each table.

title: IDOR — notes read/updated/deleted by id with no ownership predicate
evidence: GET/PATCH/DELETE each call getUser (so the caller is authenticated) then query the service-role client with .eq('id', params.id) and no owner_id check (lines 15, 30, 42) — broken object-level authorization; any signed-in user reaches any note by id.
fix: Add .eq('owner_id', user.sub) to every by-id query, or enforce via RLS.

title: Admin authorization enforced in the UI only (broken function-level authz / BFLA)
evidence: GET /api/admin/users authenticates via getUser but performs NO server-side role check before returning every profile (line 13, comment 'The admin dashboard only renders this for admins'). The only admin gate is client-side localStorage role in app/admin/page.tsx. It is authenticated-but-unauthorized, not unauthenticated.
impact: Any signed-in non-admin user lists all users by calling the endpoint directly.
fix: Assert the caller's role server-side in the handler (function-level authorization).

title: SSRF via user-supplied URL in the avatar proxy and note import
evidence: fetchRemote(url) fetches whatever URL it is given (lib/fetchUrl.ts:7). It is reached with request-controlled input from /api/avatar?url= (avatar/route.ts:6) and the /api/import body (import/route.ts:13) with no host allow-list — SSRF to cloud metadata / internal hosts.
impact: Server-side requests to attacker-chosen internal/metadata endpoints.
fix: Validate scheme + resolve and deny RFC1918/link-local hosts before fetching.

title: Stored XSS via dangerouslySetInnerHTML on the note body
evidence: note.body is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML (app/notes/[id]/page.tsx:21) — stored, attacker-controlled HTML executes in the viewer's browser.
impact: Session/credential theft against any user who views a malicious note.
fix: Render as text or sanitize with DOMPurify before injecting.

title: Mass assignment / over-posting on note writes
evidence: POST insert({ ...body, owner_id: body.owner_id ?? user.sub }) (notes/route.ts:29) and PATCH update({ ...body }) (notes/[id]/route.ts:29) spread the raw parsed request body with no field whitelist — the client can set arbitrary columns, including owner_id, enabling over-posting.
impact: Callers write attacker-chosen columns and can reassign note ownership.
fix: Pick an explicit allow-list of writable fields; never spread req.json().

title: Weak API-token randomness (Math.random) plus MD5 hashing
evidence: generateApiToken builds the token from Math.random() (tokens.ts:12) — not cryptographically random — and hashToken stores MD5(token) (tokens.ts:19), a broken hash for a security token.
impact: API tokens are predictable and their stored hashes are weak.
fix: Use crypto.randomBytes and a strong keyed hash (e.g. SHA-256/HMAC).

title: Insecure JWT — no expiry, unpinned algorithm, hardcoded fallback secret
evidence: signSession calls jwt.sign with no expiresIn (jwt.ts:17); verifySession calls jwt.verify with no algorithms allow-list (jwt.ts:23); and JWT_SECRET falls back to the hardcoded 'notevault-dev-secret' (jwt.ts:6). Three facets: non-expiring tokens, algorithm confusion, and a guessable signing secret.
fix: Set expiresIn, pin algorithms:['HS256'], and require a real secret (no fallback).

title: Wildcard CORS on the authenticated API
evidence: CORS_HEADERS sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin:'*' (object literal, cors.ts:4) and is applied to every note/admin API response.
impact: Any origin can script authenticated cross-origin calls against the API.
fix: Reflect only an explicit allow-list of origins; never '*' with credentials.

title: No CSRF protection and no rate limiting on mutating and auth routes
evidence: State-changing POST/PATCH/DELETE handlers under app/api/notes accept cross-origin requests with no CSRF/same-origin guard, and there is no rate limiting on the import or auth-adjacent paths (app/api/import/route.ts).
impact: CSRF against mutating endpoints and unbounded brute-force/abuse.
fix: Add CSRF defenses for cookie-auth paths and a shared-store rate limiter.

title: SSTI via ejs.render on a user template plus a vulnerable ejs dependency
evidence: POST /api/render calls ejs.render(String(template ?? ''), { note }) with template taken from req.json() (render/route.ts:8) — server-side template injection. The declared dependency ejs@3.1.6 (package.json) is itself known-vulnerable (SSTI/RCE advisories).
impact: Remote code execution via a crafted EJS template.
fix: Do not render user-supplied templates; upgrade ejs and use a sandboxed renderer.
